Catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation in the elderly >75 years
old: Systematic review and meta‐analysis

Introduction: Atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation is increasingly performed worldwide. As
comfort with AF ablation increases, the procedure is increasingly used in patients
that are older and in those with more comorbidities. However,
it is not well
established whether AF ablation in the elderly, especially those >75 years old, has
comparable safety and efficacy to younger populations.
Objective: To compare the efficacy and safety profiles in patients older than
75 years undergoing AF ablation with younger patients.
Methods: Databases from EMBASE, Medline, PubMed, and Cochrane, were searched
from inception through September 2021. Studies that compared the success rates in
AF catheter ablation and all complications rates between patients who were older vs
under 75 years were included. Effect estimates from the individual studies were
extracted and combined using random effect, generic inverse variance method of
DerSimonian and Laird.
Results: Twenty‐seven observational studies were included in the analysis consisting
of 363,542 patients who underwent AF ablation. Comparing patients older than
75 years old to younger patients, there was no difference in the success of ablation
rates between elderly and younger patients (pooled OR 0.85: 95% CI:0.69–1.05,
p = .131). On the other hand, AF ablation in the elderly was associated with higher
complication rates (pooled OR 1.42: 95% CI:1.21–1.68, p < .001).
Conclusion: As AF ablation is expanded to elderly populations, our study found that AF
ablation success rates were similar in both elderly and younger patients. However, older
patients experience higher rates of complications that should be considered when
Disclosures: None.
offering the procedure and as a means to improve outcomes with future innovations.

drug therapy.4,5 Outcome data derived from recent randomized
controlled trials (RCT) support catheter ablation as a first‐line therapy
in certain patients with paroxysmal AF.6,7 Despite a lower risk of AF

In summary, NOS ranged from 6 to 8, indicating moderate to high

4 | STUDY CHA RACTERISTICS AND
QUAL ITY ASS ESSM ENT
The total population in our study was 363,542 patients. As our
populations of interest were mainly elderly, which differed in
definitions from the included studies, both cutoffs aged at 75
and 80 were used dichotomously. The average age in elderly
patients was 82.9 ± 3.3 years with a cutoff at 80 while 77.9 ± 2.5
years when using a cutoff of 75. The majority of elderly
populations were female with an average CHA2DS2VASc score
of 3.8 ± 1.3.
Comparatively, there were significantly higher CHA2DS2VASc
scores and prevalence of major comorbidities including DM, CAD,
hypertension, COPD, and prior strokes in the elderly group. On the
contrary, elderly had a statistically lower BMI compared to non‐elderly
patients. However, no differences were observed on procedural time,
fluoroscopy time, mean LA size, and LVEF in both groups (p > .05)
(Data S1 and S2).
5 | ATRIA L A RRHYTHMIA ‐FR EE
SUR VIVAL RATES
5.1 | Overall
For accumulative AA‐free survival rate, there was no difference
between elderly and non‐elderly patients (pooled OR 0.85: 95% CI
0.69–1.05, p = .131). There was moderate heterogeneity in this
analysis (I2 = 41.3%). Using different age cutoffs, there remained no
differences in AA‐free survival rates (pooled OR 0.88: 95% CI
0.67–1.15, p = .336 with I2 = 43.1%, cutoff at 75 and pooled OR
0.81: 95% CI 0.57–1.15, p = .235 with I2 = 41.9%, cutoff at 80)
(Figure 2).
5.2 | Cryotherapy versus radiofrequency
From available studies with cryotherapy data, no differences
were found between elderly and non‐ elderly groups (pooled OR
0.93: 95% CI 0.69–1.27, p = .67 with I2 = 12%). Similarly, we
did not find any statistical differences in patients undergoing
radiofrequency ablation (pooled OR 0.72: 95% CI 0.48–1.08,
p = .11 with I2 = 68.4%) and in patients within study employing
both techniques (pooled OR 0.98: 95% CI 0.70–1.39, p = .93 with
(Data S1 and S2). We performed a meta‐regression
